prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Learn how to summon and control your pet on screen", "Finding & Controlling Your Desktop Pet", "Learn hotkeys to toggle pet visibility, bring your pet to focus, or move it around your desktop anytime."]
1: ["Generating Your Desktop Pet", "Your custom pet assets and animations are being rendered."]
2: ["Choose Your Companion & Story"]
3: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion", "Right-click your pet on the desktop or use key shortcuts to chat, access settings, or hide the pet anytime."]
4: ["Photo Upload Guidelines", "Use clear, well-lit photos to ensure accurate desktop pet rendering."]
5: ["Feel free to minimize. We will notify you as soon as your pet is ready on your desktop."]
6: ["Sign in with your registered email to automatically sync and restore your existing desktop pets."]
7: ["Official Desktop Pet Certificate"]
8: ["Your Virtual Desktop Buddy Awaits", "Discover how desktop pets live right on your screen while you work, study, and play."]
9: ["Preparing Desktop Pet Assets"]
